raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add `vllm run-batch --resume` for local output files. Completed successful requests are skipped; failed and missing requests run again and append results instead of truncating the output. Fixes #60184.

## Claims

- Match successful HTTP 200 responses without an error by `custom_id`.
- Preserve existing complete records and recover an incomplete final JSONL record.
- Reject duplicate input IDs and incompatible/corrupt output before model loading or output modification.
- Avoid loading a model when every input request already succeeded.

## Validation

Linux ARM64 CPU, real `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` weights:

- Before: the new end-to-end test completes its first inference run, then fails because `--resume` is unrecognized.
- After: 27 selected tests pass, including a real first run, recovery from successful/failed/partial output, and a completed-batch rerun that leaves output unchanged without loading a model.
- Existing dispatcher/writer/validation coverage and new corrupt-record, partial-UTF8, URL, duplicate-ID, and skip-completed cases pass.

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py \
  -k "resume or validate_batch or dispatch or output_writer or unwritable" -q
```

Pre-commit and MkDocs build passed. The existing launcher Buildkite step includes this test file. Initial validation used Python sources on base `db3b0f0fae4b` and CPU native extensions from wheel commit `8e2beaa3bff5`; CUDA was not exercised.

On 2026-10-29, merged `main` at `a0e31b7353cc` in `1aa17ed7`. The conflict was in `test_run_batch.py`: this PR's resume test and the `/v1/completions` test from #64097 were added at the same location. Both tests are retained unchanged, together with upstream full-URL routing.

The validation command above was extended with `or completions_endpoint or url_matches`. It passed 28 tests; the upstream completions test initially failed during model warmup because the CPU VM lacked a C++ compiler and Python development headers. After installing `g++` and `python3.12-dev`, that unchanged test passed separately:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py::test_completions_endpoint -q
# 1 passed in 16.55s
```

This gives 29 passing selected tests across the two runs, including real-model resume/retry behavior and mixed chat/completions routing with string and list prompts. Pre-commit and the MkDocs user-guide build also pass on the merged tree. Validation used Linux ARM64 CPU with the same native extensions as above; the new upstream `orjson` dependency was installed. CUDA was not exercised.

## Details

The output is scanned read-only first, recording successful IDs and the end of its last valid record. Input validation finishes before opening the output for append or trimming its partial tail. Normal runs retain their existing overwrite behavior and do not accumulate the resume ID sets.

Use the same input and model settings; ID matching cannot detect changed prompts or sampling parameters. Existing failed attempts remain in the output. New responses retain input order among pending requests. Resume requires a regular local output file and a single writer, and stores ID sets proportional to the input/output request count.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-10-21 found no matching open PR. The issue author expressed interest, and a later comment discusses flushing out-of-order completions; this PR only resumes records already on disk and leaves cancellation/write-order behavior unchanged.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement the change, tests, documentation, and validation.

@@ -289,6 +289,32 @@ vllm run-batch \
 
 See [vllm run-batch](./run-batch.md) for the full reference of all available arguments.
 
+### Resume an interrupted batch
+
+Pass `--resume` with the same input file, local output file, and model settings
+to continue an interrupted run:
+
+```bash
+vllm run-batch -i requests.jsonl -o responses.jsonl --model <model> --resume
+```
+
+Successful responses (HTTP 200 with no error) are matched by `custom_id` and
+skipped. Missing or failed requests run again, with their new responses appended
+to the output. Existing failure records remain, so an ID can have multiple
+attempts; use its successful response when reading the results. Input IDs must be
+unique. Successful output IDs absent from the input are rejected before loading
+the model.
+
+A final line interrupted during writing is discarded before appending. Malformed
+complete lines and invalid response records cause an error instead. When every
+request already succeeded, no model is loaded. A missing output file starts a
+new batch.
+
+Resume supports regular local output files only, and only one process should
+write to the file at a time. Keep the input requests and model settings unchanged:
+`custom_id` matching does not detect changed prompts or sampling parameters.
+Without `--resume`, the output file is overwritten as before.
+
 ## preload
